problem: Prior VLN methods use single-step planning, directly emitting a navigation action at each step, which does not match the naturally hierarchical process of setting and achieving sub-goals.
motivation: Navigation toward a global goal requires adaptively setting a series of sub-goals and then executing them. A planner that explicitly separates sub-goal setting from execution should fit this process better and give supervision signals at each stage.
key_idea: Split VLN into high-level sub-goal setting via adaptive zone partition and selection, and low-level multi-step execution inside the chosen zone, switching between them asynchronously and training with hierarchical RL.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that explicit two-level planning with on-the-fly scene-aware zones, plus stage-specific supervision from HRL and curriculum-based auxiliary losses, gives better results than single-step planning.
method: State-Switcher Module (SSM): asynchronously switches between high-level zone-setting actions and low-level execution actions.
Scene-aware adaptive Zone Partition (SZP): divides the whole navigation area into zones on-the-fly as the scene is explored.
Goal-oriented Zone Selection (GZS): selects the zone that serves as the current sub-goal, based on the instruction and goal.
Low-level execution: the agent takes multiple navigation-decision steps within the selected zone.
Hierarchical RL (HRL) training: gives effective supervision to each stage, combined with auxiliary losses and curriculum learning.
